docs.title: Customers Frontend — Design Spec
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-02 Status: Approved for planning

docs.title: Intent
docs.text:
Build a Vite + React + TypeScript frontend that exposes the backend Customer 360 REST API. The first deliverable is the Customers page: a table of customers with per-row actions to view, edit, and delete a record. Edit (and create) open a separate form page. A shared header and a left sidebar (Customers / Accounts / Transactions) frame every page.

Audience: internal demo of the C360 streaming pipeline. Success = a user can browse the customer list, view a customer's detail, create a customer, edit an existing one, and delete one, all against the live FastAPI backend.

docs.title: Stack Decisions
docs.text:
• Language: TypeScript (Vite react-ts template).
  • Styling: Plain CSS. Icons from lucide-react.
  • Data layer: Native fetch wrapped in a small typed API module. No TanStack Query / axios.
  • Backend wiring: Enable CORS on the FastAPI backend for the Vite dev origin (http://localhost:5173). No Vite proxy.
  • Routing: react-router-dom.

docs.title: Backend Contract (existing)
docs.text:
Base path: /api/v1/customers (FastAPI, see apps/backend/api/customer_resource.py).

  • GET /api/v1/customers → Customer[]
  • GET /api/v1/customers/{id} → Customer (404 if missing)
  • POST /api/v1/customers → Customer (201)
  • PUT /api/v1/customers/{id} → Customer (200, 404 if missing)
  • DELETE /api/v1/customers/{id} → 204 (404 if missing)

Customer fields (from apps/backend/customers/models.py):

field type notes customer_id UUID server-assigned first_name string required last_name string required email string required phone string? date_of_birth datetime? edited via date input gender string? address_line1 string? address_line2 string? city string? state string? postal_code string? country string default "US" customer_since date default today segment string? status string default "ACTIVE" created_at datetime server-assigned, read-only updated_at datetime server-assigned, read-only

CustomerCreate = all fields except the server-assigned ones. CustomerUpdate = same fields, all optional.

docs.title: Directory Layout
docs.text:
apps/frontend/
  package.json
  tsconfig.json
  vite.config.ts
  index.html
  src/
    main.tsx                 # bootstrap + <BrowserRouter>
    App.tsx                  # routes inside <AppLayout>
    config.ts                # API base URL (import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL)
    api/client.ts            # fetch wrapper: base URL, JSON, error handling
    api/customers.ts         # listCustomers/getCustomer/createCustomer/updateCustomer/deleteCustomer
    types/customer.ts        # Customer, CustomerCreate, CustomerUpdate
    components/
      AppLayout.tsx          # Header + Sidebar + <Outlet/> content area
      Header.tsx             # app title, shared across pages
      Sidebar.tsx            # nav links w/ active state
      ConfirmDialog.tsx      # reusable confirm modal (used for delete)
    pages/
      CustomersPage.tsx      # table + row actions + "Add customer"
      CustomerDetailPage.tsx # read-only detail view
      CustomerFormPage.tsx   # create AND edit form
      PlaceholderPage.tsx    # "coming soon" for Accounts/Transactions
    styles/
      index.css              # base + layout
      (component-scoped css as needed)

docs.title: Routes
docs.text: path page notes / — redirect to /customers /customers CustomersPage table view + Add button /customers/new CustomerFormPage create mode (no id) /customers/:id CustomerDetailPage view icon target /customers/:id/edit CustomerFormPage edit mode (loads record) /accounts PlaceholderPage "coming soon" /transactions PlaceholderPage "coming soon"

docs.title: Components & Responsibilities
docs.text:
• AppLayout — fixed header on top, fixed sidebar on left, scrollable content region rendering <Outlet/>. Pure layout, no data.
  • Header — static app title/branding. No props needed initially.
  • Sidebar — three NavLinks (Customers, Accounts, Transactions) with active styling. Icons from lucide-react.
  • ConfirmDialog — props: open, title, message, onConfirm, onCancel. Reusable; used by CustomersPage for delete.
  • CustomersPage — fetches list on mount; holds loading/error/data state. Renders table columns: Name (first + last), Email, Phone, Segment, Status, Actions (view/edit/delete icons). Delete opens ConfirmDialog, calls deleteCustomer, then refetches. "Add customer" button → /customers/new.
  • CustomerDetailPage — fetches one by id; renders read-only field list; "Edit" and "Back" actions.
  • CustomerFormPage — controlled form over editable fields. If :id present: fetch record, populate, submit via updateCustomer (PUT). Else: blank form, submit via createCustomer (POST). Client-side required-field validation for first_name, last_name, email. On success → navigate /customers. Shows submit error inline.
  • PlaceholderPage — generic "coming soon" with a title prop.

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text:
• config.ts: API_BASE_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE_URL ?? "http://localhost:8000/api/v1".
  • api/client.ts: request<T>(path, options) — prefixes base URL, sets JSON headers, throws a typed ApiError (status + message) on non-2xx, returns parsed JSON (or undefined for 204).
  • api/customers.ts: the five CRUD functions, typed against types/customer.ts.

docs.title: Error & Loading Handling
docs.text:
• List/detail pages render a loading indicator while fetching and an error message (with the API message) on failure.
  • Form submit failures render inline near the submit button; the form stays populated.
  • Delete failures surface a message and leave the row intact.

docs.title: Backend Change
docs.text: Add fastapi.middleware.cors.CORSMiddleware to apps/backend/main.py: allow origin http://localhost:5173 (dev), methods GET,POST,PUT,DELETE, all headers. Keep it minimal and dev-oriented.

docs.title: Out of Scope (YAGNI)
docs.text:
• Authentication / authorization.
  • Pagination, sorting, search/filter (list endpoint returns all records).
  • Accounts and Transactions data pages (no backend yet — placeholders only).
  • State caching libraries, optimistic updates.
  • Production build/deploy pipeline and Dockerization.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Component/unit tests with Vitest + React Testing Library:
  • api/customers.ts builds correct requests (mock fetch).
  • CustomersPage renders rows from mocked list and triggers delete flow.
  • CustomerFormPage validates required fields and calls create vs update based on presence of id.
  • Manual verification against the running backend for the full CRUD loop.

docs.title: Kafka Produce Config — Design Spec
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-02 Status: Approved for planning

docs.title: Intent
docs.text:
Let the user control, at runtime, whether the backend also emits a Kafka event when a record is created, updated, or deleted — without changing the system of record (PostgreSQL). Exposed as a config REST API and a Settings page in the frontend.

Audience: internal C360 demo. Success = a user can open a Settings page, flip a single "Produce Kafka events on changes" switch, and have subsequent customer create/update/delete operations emit (or not emit) Kafka events accordingly, with the setting surviving a backend restart.

docs.title: Decisions (from brainstorming)
docs.text:
• Behavior model: dual-write. PostgreSQL stays the store. When the flag is ON, create/update/delete in the postgres path ALSO emit a Kafka event.
  • Granularity: single global switch — one boolean covering create, update, and delete together.
  • Persistence: JSON file on disk — survives restarts.
  • Default: OFF — normal postgres operation requires no Kafka creds.
  • SINK=kafka path unchanged — producing is intrinsic to that mode; the toggle governs only the postgres (dual-write) path.
  • Best-effort emission — if a Kafka produce fails (e.g. no creds, broker unreachable), log a warning and still return success for the DB operation.
  • Frontend: auto-save — flipping the switch immediately PUTs the config.

docs.title: Config model & store
docs.text:
New module apps/backend/config_store.py:

  • AppConfig (pydantic BaseModel): kafka_produce_enabled: bool = False.
  • JSON file path from settings.RUNTIME_CONFIG_FILE, defaulting to runtime_config.json next to the backend. The file is gitignored.
  • get_config() -> AppConfig: returns the in-memory config, loading from the file on first call; if the file is missing or unreadable, returns the default and does not raise.
  • set_config(config: AppConfig) -> AppConfig: updates the in-memory config and writes it to the file; returns the stored config.
  • Single-process assumption (one uvicorn worker); no locking needed.

Add to apps/backend/config.py Settings: RUNTIME_CONFIG_FILE: str | None = None (when None, the store uses its default path).

docs.title: Config REST API
docs.text:
New apps/backend/api/config_resource.py, router prefix /config, included under /api/v1 in main.py:

  • GET /api/v1/config → AppConfig (200).
  • PUT /api/v1/config body AppConfig → AppConfig (200), persisted.

docs.title: Kafka producer
docs.text: apps/backend/customers/kafka_producer.py: add produce_delete(customer: Customer) -> None mirroring produce_create / produce_update, with op="D".

docs.title: Service wiring
docs.text:
apps/backend/customers/service.py: in the postgres branch of create, update, and delete_by_id, after a successful DB operation and when get_config().kafka_produce_enabled is True, emit the matching Kafka event via a best-effort helper:

def _maybe_emit(op, customer):   # op in {"C","U","D"}
    if not config_store.get_config().kafka_produce_enabled:
        return
    try:
        <produce_create|produce_update|produce_delete>(customer)
    except Exception:
        logger.warning("kafka emit failed for op=%s id=%s", op, id, exc_info=True)
  • create: emit "C" with the returned Customer.
  • update: emit "U" with the returned Customer (skip when update returned None / no row).
  • delete_by_id: emit "D" — the delete path must fetch the customer before deletion so a full Customer payload is available for the event; emit only when a row was actually deleted.

The SINK=kafka branch is unchanged.

docs.title: Types & API
docs.text:
• apps/frontend/src/types/config.ts: AppConfig { kafka_produce_enabled: boolean }.
  • apps/frontend/src/api/config.ts:
  • getConfig(): Promise<AppConfig> → GET /config.
  • updateConfig(data: AppConfig): Promise<AppConfig> → PUT /config.

docs.title: Settings page
docs.text:
apps/frontend/src/pages/ConfigPage.tsx:

  • Fetches config on mount; loading and error states (reuse existing status-msg styles).
  • Renders a labeled toggle switch "Produce Kafka events on create / update / delete" bound to kafka_produce_enabled.
  • Auto-saves on flip: optimistic UI update, PUT, and on failure revert the switch and show an error message.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
• Sidebar.tsx: add a fourth link, "Settings" (lucide Settings gear icon) → /settings.
  • App.tsx: add route /settings → ConfigPage.

docs.title: Error & Loading Handling
docs.text:
• Config page shows a loading indicator while fetching and an error message (with the API message) on GET or PUT failure; a failed PUT reverts the toggle to its last known value.
  • Backend GET never fails on a missing file (returns default). PUT failures (e.g. unwritable file) surface as a 500 via the normal FastAPI path.

docs.title: Out of Scope (YAGNI)
docs.text:
• Per-table or per-operation granularity (single global switch only).
  • Multi-worker / multi-instance config sharing (single-process assumption).
  • Authentication on the config endpoints.
  • Toggling the SINK=kafka path's intrinsic production.
  • A Kafka connectivity/health check in the UI.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Backend (pytest, infra-free using the existing SINK=kafka harness pattern where an app is needed; config store tested directly):

  • config_store: default when file absent; set_config then get_config round-trips through the file; corrupt/unreadable file falls back to default without raising.
  • Config API: GET returns current; PUT updates and persists (a subsequent GET reflects it).
  • Service gating (postgres path, db_sink mocked): flag ON → the matching producer is called on create/update/delete; flag OFF → producer not called; producer raising → the service call still returns the DB result (best-effort).

Frontend (vitest + RTL):

  • api/config.ts: getConfig/updateConfig hit the right paths/verbs.
  • ConfigPage: renders the current value from a mocked getConfig; flipping the switch calls updateConfig with the new value; a failed updateConfig reverts the switch and shows an error.

docs.title: Accounts (Backend + Frontend) — Design Spec
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-04 Status: Approved for planning

docs.title: Intent
docs.text:
Add an Accounts resource mirroring the existing Customers pattern: a Postgres CRUD REST API with config-gated best-effort Kafka (Debezium) emission, and frontend pages (table with view/edit/delete, detail, create/edit form). An account belongs to a customer.

Audience: internal C360 demo. Success = a user can list/view/create/edit/ delete accounts in the UI against the live backend, and — when the existing Settings "Produce Kafka events" toggle is ON — each account create/update/ delete also emits a Debezium envelope to the accounts topic (best-effort).

docs.title: Decisions (from brainstorming)
docs.text:
• Full parity with customers: Postgres storage + config-gated dual-write Kafka emission using the real schema the user added (accounts/schema/schema-cdc.public.accounts-value-v1.avsc, a full Debezium cdc.public.accounts.Envelope).
  • Skip the SINK=kafka CSV-inventory mode for accounts (no seed CSV). Accounts storage is always Postgres; the toggle governs the postgres path.
  • The existing global Settings toggle (kafka_produce_enabled) now also governs accounts emission (no new toggle).
  • balance/credit_limit are float in the Pydantic models, converted to Decimal (precision 18, scale 2) when building the Avro payload.
  • Owning customer chosen in the form via a dropdown of customers.
  • Reuse the customers producer's resilience fixes: bounded flush_timeout and an on_delivery logging callback; emission failures are logged and never fail (or hang) the DB operation.

docs.title: Backend Contract (new)
docs.text:
Base path /api/v1/accounts (FastAPI), mirroring the customers resource:

  • POST /api/v1/accounts → Account (201); 409 on duplicate account_number.
  • GET /api/v1/accounts → Account[].
  • GET /api/v1/accounts/{id} → Account (404 if missing).
  • PUT /api/v1/accounts/{id} → Account (200, 404 if missing).
  • DELETE /api/v1/accounts/{id} → 204 (404 if missing).

Account fields (from the accounts DDL in scripts/db/create_tables.py):

field type notes account_id UUID server-assigned customer_id UUID required (FK → customers) account_number string required, unique account_type string required (CHECKING/SAVINGS/CREDIT/LOAN) currency string default "USD" balance float default 0.0 (DB NUMERIC(18,2)) credit_limit float? optional opened_date date default today closed_date date? optional status string default "ACTIVE" created_at datetime server-assigned, read-only updated_at datetime server-assigned, read-only

AccountCreate = all except server-assigned. AccountUpdate = all optional.

docs.title: Backend Structure (mirrors customers/)
docs.text:
apps/backend/accounts/
  __init__.py
  models.py        # AccountCreate / AccountUpdate / Account (pydantic)
  db_sink.py       # psycopg2 pool (reuse pattern), accounts DDL, CRUD
  kafka_producer.py# Debezium envelope producer for accounts
  service.py       # CRUD dispatch + _maybe_emit (config-gated, bounded flush)
apps/backend/api/account_resource.py   # APIRouter(prefix="/accounts")

docs.title: models.py
docs.text: Mirror customers/models.py: AccountCreate(BaseModel) with the create fields and defaults (currency="USD", balance=0.0, country-style defaults: opened_date: date = date.today(), status="ACTIVE"); AccountUpdate all-optional; Account(AccountCreate) adds account_id, created_at, updated_at with model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True).

docs.title: db_sink.py
docs.text: Mirror customers/db_sink.py: - Lazy SimpleConnectionPool from settings.DATABASE_URL (reuse the exact _ensure_pool/_get_conn/_put_conn pattern). - init_db() runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (...) matching the DDL verbatim, the idx_accounts_customer_id index, and the trg_accounts_updated_at trigger (the set_updated_at function already exists from the customers init; use CREATE OR REPLACE/guarded trigger). - create, update, get_by_id, list_all (ORDER BY created_at DESC), delete_by_id — same shapes as customers, returning Account. create maps psycopg2.errors.UniqueViolation → HTTPException(409, "An account with that account number already exists"). - No seed_from_csv (accounts has no seed file).

docs.title: kafka_producer.py
docs.text: Mirror customers/kafka_producer.py (the current, fixed version): - Load _SCHEMA_STR from accounts/schema/schema-cdc.public.accounts-value-v1.avsc. - Debezium op codes c/u/d; synthetic source block with table="accounts"; topic from settings.KAFKA_TOPIC_ACCOUNTS. - _build_value(account) encodes: UUIDs as strings; opened_date/ closed_date via _to_debezium_date; created_at/updated_at via _to_debezium_ts; balance/credit_limit as Decimal quantized to 2 places (the Avro connect.data.Decimal, scale 2 — None for a missing credit_limit); strings passed through. - _build_envelope(account, op) identical structure (before/after/source/ op/ts_ms/transaction). - _on_delivery logging callback; _produce(account, op, flush_timeout=None) with the same bounded-flush semantics; produce_create/update/delete wrappers accepting flush_timeout.

docs.title: service.py
docs.text: Mirror the customers service's postgres path + emission: - create/update/get_by_id/list_all/delete_by_id route to db_sink (Postgres only — no SINK dispatch for accounts). - _maybe_emit(op, account) — gated by config_store.get_config() .kafka_produce_enabled; calls the matching kafka_producer.produce_* with flush_timeout=_EMIT_FLUSH_TIMEOUT (5.0); wraps in try/except and logs on failure (best-effort, never fails/hangs the DB op). - create emits "c"; update emits "u" when a row is returned; delete_by_id fetches the account (via get_by_id) before deleting and emits "d" only when a row was actually deleted.

docs.title: Config & wiring
docs.text:
• config.py: add KAFKA_TOPIC_ACCOUNTS: str = "cdc.public.accounts".
  • main.py: import and include_router(account_router, prefix="/api/v1"); in lifespan (postgres branch) call accounts_db_sink.init_db() AFTER db_sink.init_db() (customers first, FK order).

docs.title: Frontend (mirrors customers pages)
docs.text:
apps/frontend/src/types/account.ts        # Account / AccountCreate / AccountUpdate
apps/frontend/src/api/accounts.ts         # list/get/create/update/delete
apps/frontend/src/pages/AccountsPage.tsx      # table + row actions
apps/frontend/src/pages/AccountDetailPage.tsx # read-only detail
apps/frontend/src/pages/AccountFormPage.tsx   # create AND edit

docs.title: Routes (App.tsx)
docs.text:
path page /accounts AccountsPage (replaces the PlaceholderPage) /accounts/new AccountFormPage (create) /accounts/:id AccountDetailPage /accounts/:id/edit AccountFormPage (edit)

The Sidebar already links /accounts; no sidebar change needed.

docs.title: Types
docs.text: account.ts: AccountCreate { customer_id: string; account_number: string; account_type: string; currency?: string | null; balance?: number | null; credit_limit?: number | null; opened_date?: string | null; closed_date?: string | null; status?: string | null }; AccountUpdate = Partial<AccountCreate>; Account extends AccountCreate { account_id: string; created_at: string; updated_at: string }.

docs.title: API module
docs.text: accounts.ts reuses request from ./client: listAccounts, getAccount, createAccount, updateAccount, deleteAccount — same shapes as customers.ts, paths under /accounts.

docs.title: AccountsPage
docs.text: Mirror CustomersPage: fetch list on mount; loading/error states; table columns Account #, Type, Customer, Balance, Status, Actions (view/edit/delete icons); delete via the shared ConfirmDialog then refetch; "Add account" button → /accounts/new. The Customer column shows the owning customer's "First Last" — to render it, the page also fetches customers once and builds a customer_id → name map (falls back to the raw id when not found).

docs.title: AccountDetailPage
docs.text: Mirror CustomerDetailPage: fetch one by id; read-only field list; Edit and Back actions. Show the customer's name (fetched) alongside the id.

docs.title: AccountFormPage (create + edit)
docs.text: Mirror CustomerFormPage, including the omit-empty-fields payload rule (send only non-empty fields so backend defaults apply — the fix that resolved the customers 422). Specifics: - Fetches customers on mount to populate a customer dropdown (required); options show "First Last — email", value = customer_id. - account_type select (CHECKING/SAVINGS/CREDIT/LOAN); status select (ACTIVE/CLOSED/FROZEN — ACTIVE default); currency text (default USD). - balance/credit_limit number inputs; opened_date/closed_date date inputs (date values trimmed to yyyy-MM-dd on load, as in customers). - Required-field validation: customer_id, account_number, account_type. - Create → POST; with :id → load + PUT. On success navigate /accounts. Submit errors shown inline (e.g. the 409 duplicate account number).

docs.title: Error & Loading Handling
docs.text: Same as customers: list/detail pages show loading + error (API message); form submit failures render inline and keep the form populated; delete failures surface a message and leave the row intact.

docs.title: Out of Scope (YAGNI)
docs.text:
• SINK=kafka CSV-inventory mode for accounts.
  • Transactions resource (separate future work; its schema was added but is not part of this spec).
  • Editing balance via dedicated money-movement semantics (balance is a plain editable field here).
  • Auth, pagination, search.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Backend (pytest, infra-free — no DB, no live Kafka): - accounts/models: defaults and optionality. - accounts.service emission gating (db_sink + producer patched on the service module): create/update/delete emit the matching producer when the flag is ON and flush_timeout is bounded; nothing emitted when OFF; update with no row does not emit; delete fetches before deleting and emits only when a row was deleted; a producer exception still returns the DB result. - accounts.kafka_producer: _build_value/envelope encodes a Decimal balance and op codes correctly (producer mocked via _get_producer). - Accounts API via a bare FastAPI() app mounting the router (no main import), with db_sink functions patched — GET/POST/PUT/DELETE happy paths and 404s; this keeps the test infra-free and avoids polluting the test_customers_kafka module graph.

Frontend (vitest + RTL), mirroring customers: - api/accounts.ts builds correct requests. - AccountsPage renders rows (customer name resolved) and runs the delete flow. - AccountDetailPage renders fields and handles 404. - AccountFormPage validates required fields, omits empty fields, populates the customer dropdown, and calls create vs update based on :id.

docs.title: Statement Graph Page — Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-22 Status: Draft — awaiting approval Repo: stream_house_c360_demo

docs.title: Intent & Why
docs.text:
The frontend (apps/frontend) is a demo tool for solution engineers showing off "the art of the possible" with Confluent Cloud + CLI + REST API. Today it has CRUD pages for Customers / Accounts / Transactions. We are adding a new section that visualizes a data product as the graph of deployed Flink statements that build it, with live status and metrics pulled from the Confluent Cloud REST API.

The demo narrative the page must support:

  1. SE opens Data Products in the left nav → sees the list (just c360 today).
  2. Selects c360 → sees the statement DAG, and at a glance that everything is green and flowing (the hero moment).
  3. Drills into one node → sees that statement's Confluent metrics.

The topology is stable, so it is served as static backend metadata. The dynamic layer — per-statement status and lag/metrics — comes from the Confluent Cloud REST API through a backend proxy (keeps the Flink/Cloud API keys server-side).

docs.title: Topology (verified against the repo)
docs.text:
The c360 pipeline deploys 8 Flink statements in 4 dependency layers (names + edges from pipelines/models/deploy_manifest.json and the ref()/source() calls in pipelines/models/c360/**/*.sql). The earlier src_dedup_* names were stale target/compiled/ artifacts and are not deployed.

  • CDC sources (topics, not statements): cdc.public.customers, cdc.public.accounts, cdc.public.transactions.
  • Layer 1 — src_*: src_customers ← customers, src_accounts ← accounts, src_transactions ← transactions.
  • Layer 2 — dim_*: dim_customers ← src_customers; dim_transactions ← src_transactions; dim_account_tx_agg ← src_accounts + dim_transactions.
  • Layer 3 — leaves: dim_tx_x_account ← dim_customers + dim_account_tx_agg; fct_c360_profile ← dim_transactions + dim_customers.

Terminal data-product node (user decision): fct_c360_profile — the named fact. It is currently a stub (projects only customer_id, first_name, last_name); building it out is out of scope here, but it is the designated "product" node the drill-down narrative builds toward. dim_tx_x_account is the other leaf and is rendered as a normal statement node.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• A Data Products left-nav entry → a list page → a per-product graph page.
  • Graph renders the c360 topology as a layered DAG of all 8 statements (4 layers, left→right), with the three CDC source topics as upstream nodes.
  • Node color = status applies to statements; the CDC source/sink topic nodes render neutral ("connected", not green/red). Statement status: green = RUNNING, amber = lag/degraded, red = FAILED/STOPPED. Animated edges convey "flowing". (A topic-level activity signal could color topics later — out of scope now.)
  • A health summary bar at the top of the graph counting statements ("7 / 8 RUNNING · 1 with lag · refreshed Ns ago") — confirmed as a key element.
  • Click a node → drill-down panel with Confluent metrics: status, uptime, messages in/s, messages out/s, pending records (lag), compute pool used, and the statement SQL.
  • A mock / offline mode so "green and flowing" is guaranteed during a live demo even with no cloud connectivity, and a live mode that calls Confluent.
  • Status auto-refreshes on a short interval to make the graph feel live.

docs.title: Non-Goals (this iteration)
docs.text:
• No write/control actions (no start/stop/resume statements from the UI) — read-only.
  • No historical time-series charts in the drill-down — current/point-in-time metrics only (the mockup's SQL + metric rows, not sparklines).
  • One data product (c360); the list is built to hold more but only c360 ships.
  • No per-statement exception/stack-trace viewer (could be a later add).
  • No frontend auth / multi-tenant concerns.

docs.title: Anti-Goals (what makes this a failure even if it "works")
docs.text:
• A demo that breaks or shows red because of transient cloud/network issues — mock mode must make the happy path deterministic.
  • Secrets in the frontend — the browser must never see a Confluent API key; all Confluent calls go through the backend proxy.
  • A graph that is hand-maintained in two places — the node/edge topology has a single source of truth (the backend descriptor, see below).

docs.title: Constraints & Existing Structure
docs.text:
• Frontend: React 19 + Vite 8, react-router-dom 7, lucide-react, plain CSS in src/styles/index.css (no CSS framework). Pages under src/pages, routed in src/App.tsx inside AppLayout; nav in src/components/Sidebar.tsx. API calls go through src/api/client.ts → request<T>() against VITE_API_BASE_URL (default http://localhost:8000/api/v1). Tests use Vitest + Testing Library; existing pages each have a .test.tsx.
  • Backend: FastAPI, routers under apps/backend/api/* mounted at /api/v1, CORS allows http://localhost:5173. config.py::Settings (pydantic-settings) already loads Kafka + Schema Registry creds from env; uv is the runner.
  • Topology source: dbt/Flink project under pipelines/. The DAG (pipelines/target/manifest.json, pipelines/models/deploy_manifest.json): sources cdc.public.{customers,accounts,transactions} → statements src_{customers,accounts,transactions} (+ src_dedup_*). Deployed statement names follow the deploy_manifest.json pattern, e.g. models-c360-sources-pipeline-src-dedup-customers.
  • Confluent posture (from CLAUDE.md): credentials are referenced from ~/.confluent/.env; never write literal keys into code or committed files.

docs.title: D1. Graph library — React Flow (@xyflow/react) with a layered layout
docs.text: Not currently a dependency. Standard fit for React 19 interactive DAGs; supports custom nodes (status color + lag badge) and a right-side panel. Because the real topology is a 4-layer DAG (not three flat lanes), node positions come from a layered/left-to-right layout — dagre (or @dagrejs/dagre) to compute coordinates, or React Flow's layouting example. (My call.)

docs.title: D2. Topology as a committed backend descriptor file
docs.text: A single source of truth: apps/backend/data_products/c360.json, hand-authored from the verified topology above (it could later be generated from the dbt manifest). It encodes nodes (id, type ∈ source|statement, label, the deployed statement name from deploy_manifest.json, the backing topic, and a is_product flag on fct_c360_profile) and edges. The backend serves it verbatim. The deployed statement names are known (pattern models-c360-<subdir>-pipeline-<model>), so no naming guess remains. (My call; topology confirmed with the user.)

docs.title: D3. Backend proxy with a GRAPH_DATA_MODE toggle: mock | live (mock-first)
docs.text: New settings in config.py: GRAPH_DATA_MODE (default mock so a fresh clone demos green out of the box), plus live-mode config: CONFLUENT_CLOUD_API_KEY/SECRET (Metrics API), FLINK_API_KEY/SECRET, FLINK_ORG_ID, FLINK_ENV_ID, FLINK_COMPUTE_POOL_ID, FLINK_REST_ENDPOINT (region host). All read from env (~/.confluent/.env style); none committed. - mock mode: status/metrics come from a deterministic in-repo fixture (everything RUNNING, realistic rates, zero/low lag). The mockup's amber "lagging" node is a mock preset variant so the SE can show the unhappy state on demand (e.g. GRAPH_DATA_MODE=mock-lag), but the default preset is all-green. - live mode (best-effort): the 8 statements are not confirmed deployed/running in the target env yet (user), and two models are unfinished — fct_c360_profile is a stub and dim_account_tx_agg may have an invalid clause order — so live mode could legitimately return non-RUNNING/red for some nodes. Therefore mock is the primary demo path; live mode is wired but best-effort and status-only-tolerant: it maps whatever Confluent returns to the common shape, and where a metric is unavailable it returns null and the UI shows "—" rather than failing. Mock remains the default so a fresh clone demos green. (My call, per user's "mock-first" decision.)

docs.title: D4. Confluent REST endpoints used in live mode
docs.text:
• Statement status: Flink SQL REST API — list/get statements under the org/env, read status.phase (RUNNING / PENDING / DEGRADED / FAILED / STOPPED / …).
  • Metrics (rates, pending records/lag, compute pool): Confluent Cloud Metrics API (api.telemetry.confluent.cloud/v2/metrics/.../query) with Flink metric descriptors, filtered by compute pool / statement.
  • Exact metric descriptor names are an implementation detail the builder must verify against current Confluent docs (e.g. records-in/out and pending-records metrics). Where a per-second rate isn't exposed directly, derive it from counter deltas between polls. (My call; naming flagged for the builder.)

docs.title: D5. Routing, nav, and refresh
docs.text:
• Nav: add Data Products to Sidebar.tsx (lucide icon, e.g. Workflow/Share2).
  • Routes in App.tsx: /data-products (list) and /data-products/:id (graph).
  • The graph page polls status every 5s (drives node colors, health bar, and the "refreshed Ns ago" label). The drill-down metrics fetch on node selection and refresh on the same interval while a node is open. (My call.)

docs.title: D6. Visual style
docs.text: Match the existing plain-CSS look; add graph/panel styles to src/styles/index.css following the mockup (lanes, status dots, health pills, metric rows, dark SQL box). No new CSS framework. (My call.)

docs.title: Backend API (new router, apps/backend/api/data_product_resource.py, /api/v1)
docs.text:
All responses are JSON; mock and live modes return identical shapes.

  • GET /data-products → [{ id, name, description, statement_count }] (from descriptor files).
  • GET /data-products/{id}/graph → { nodes: [{ id, type, label, statement_name, topic }], edges: [{ source, target }] } (static descriptor, D2).
  • GET /data-products/{id}/status → [{ node_id, statement_name, phase, lagging: bool }] for statement nodes only (source/sink topic nodes carry no phase and render neutral), plus a rollup the health bar uses (running, total, lagging) counted over statements. Drives node coloring. (mock or live.)
  • GET /data-products/{id}/nodes/{node_id}/metrics → { status, uptime_seconds, messages_in_per_sec, messages_out_per_sec, pending_records, compute_pool_cfu, sql }. (mock or live.)

Live-mode Confluent calls live behind a small client module (apps/backend/confluent/), unit-tested with mocked HTTP; the resource layer never talks to Confluent directly.

docs.title: Frontend pieces
docs.text:
• src/api/dataProducts.ts — typed wrappers over the four endpoints (via request<T>()).
  • src/types/dataProduct.ts — DataProduct, GraphNode, GraphEdge, NodeStatus, NodeMetrics.
  • src/pages/DataProductsPage.tsx — list (table like the existing pages), row → /data-products/:id.
  • src/pages/StatementGraphPage.tsx — React Flow DAG (custom status-colored node), health bar, selection → drill-down panel; 5s polling.
  • src/components/Sidebar.tsx — new nav entry; src/App.tsx — two routes.
  • Styles appended to src/styles/index.css.
  • Vitest tests alongside new pages/api (mirroring existing .test.tsx convention), mocking the api module; assert health rollup, node coloring by status, and panel rendering from a fixture.

docs.title: What's Left to the Builder
docs.text:
• Verify exact Confluent Metrics API descriptor names and the Flink Statements API path/version against current docs (D4); implement rate derivation where needed.
  • Decide the precise uptime source (statement createdAt/updated timestamp vs a metric) in live mode.
  • Choose the exact lucide icon and finalize spacing/CSS to match the house style.
  • Author the committed c360.json descriptor from the verified topology (8 statements, edges, is_product on fct_c360_profile, backing topic per node).
  • Wire GRAPH_DATA_MODE presets (mock, mock-lag, live) and document the env vars in apps/backend/.env.example (names only, no secrets).
  • In live mode, tolerate unhealthy/unfinished statements gracefully (null metrics → "—"); do not let a FAILED statement break the page.

docs.title: Resolved Decisions (from brainstorming)
docs.text:
• Topology verified against the repo: 8 statements, 4 layers (see Topology section). The src_dedup_* names were stale artifacts and are dropped.
  • Terminal data-product node: fct_c360_profile (user), rendered with an is_product flag; it is a stub today and building it out is out of scope.
  • Live mode: mock-first; live is best-effort and metric-tolerant (user).
  • Topic nodes (CDC sources / sink) render neutral; status color is for statements.

docs.title: CRM analytics data products → dashboard via snapshot queries
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-29 Status: Draft for approval

docs.title: Intent and why
docs.text:
The C360 analytics dashboard (GET /analytics/c360-profile) currently pulls every customer row of fct_c360_profile over the wire (up to ANALYTICS_SNAPSHOT_LIMIT = 50_000) and folds the aggregates in Python (analytics/aggregate.py). That contradicts the demo's thesis — build the analytics as data products in Flink and expose them through a simple query.

The aggregates now exist as a dedicated crm Flink data product (five streaming_table models, already deployed). This change rewires the dashboard's live path to run five trivial snapshot SELECTs against those tables and assemble the response — so Flink does the aggregation and only summary rows cross the wire. The snapshot queries are issued through the official confluent-sql DB-API driver (per the maintainer's direction to use it).

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Live dashboard aggregates come from the crm tables, not Python folding.
  • Snapshot queries run through confluent-sql (snapshot-mode cursors).
  • The HTTP response shape is unchanged (frontend keeps working), except the payload model is renamed C360Analytics → DataAnalytics.
  • Mock mode keeps working with zero infra (unchanged default).
  • Failure-tolerant: an unconfigured/failed live query yields an empty payload (row_count == 0), never a 500 — matching today's contract.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Changing the crm Flink SQL / contracts. They are built, deployed, and (per the maintainer) the earlier by_gender/by_country swap is already fixed. This doc treats them as a fixed upstream.
  • Migrating the per-customer paths (search_customers, get_customer_profile, and their RTCE/Lightning variants) to confluent-sql. They keep using FlinkSnapshotClient / LightningClient. (Can follow later.)
  • Changing the HTTP route path /analytics/c360-profile or the frontend API function name getC360Analytics. Only the payload type is renamed. (See "Calls I made" — open to widening if desired.)

docs.title: Anti-goals (would make this a failure even if it "works")
docs.text:
• Mock mode requiring any Flink/Confluent configuration to render.
  • A live-query failure turning into a dashboard error instead of an empty state.
  • Numbers that silently disagree with what aggregate() produced for the same data (the mock path stays the behavioural reference).

docs.title: Current state (as of this doc)
docs.text:
• api/analytics_resource.py::get_c360_profile → service.get_c360_analytics() → providers.get_rows() (mock fixture or full-table FlinkSnapshotClient.snapshot) → aggregate(rows).
  • confluent-sql is not yet a dependency.
  • Config already carries every coordinate confluent_sql.connect() needs (FLINK_ORG_ID, FLINK_ENV_ID, CLOUD_PROVIDER, CLOUD_REGION, FLINK_COMPUTE_POOL_ID, FLINK_API_KEY/SECRET, FLINK_DATABASE).

docs.title: The data products (fixed upstream — reference)
docs.text:
All in pipelines/models/crm/facts/, streaming_table, upsert changelog, avro-registry, each distributed by its PK. Built from fct_c360_profile.

Table PK Columns Feeds fct_crm_summary qscope='ALL' total_customers, total_accounts, total_balance, total_transactions, total_txn_amount, avg_age, missing_email, missing_phone, complete all scalar KPIs + data_quality fct_crm_by_segment customer_segment customer_count, total_balance by_segment and balance_by_segment fct_crm_by_generation generation_segment generation_count by_generation fct_crm_by_gender gender gender_count by_gender fct_crm_by_country country country_count by_country

Derived, not stored: avg_balance_per_customer = total_balance / total_customers (computed in the backend). by_country is trimmed to top-8 + "Other" in the backend (the table stays full-fidelity).

docs.title: New: confluent-sql dependency
docs.text: Add confluent-sql to apps/backend/pyproject.toml dependencies. import confluent_sql.

docs.title: New: analytics/confluent_sql_client.py — ConfluentSqlClient
docs.text:
Snapshot semantics (resolved by research, confirm with a live probe): confluent-sql defaults to snapshot mode, which uses Confluent Cloud's native snapshot query — it returns the table's current state (one latest row per PK) as a finite result set and terminates. This is why it replaces the changelog-draining in FlinkSnapshotClient: no collapse_changelog, no long-poll loop, no row cap. Residual risk until probed live (see "Spike" below).

Catalog/database: the catalog is the environment, resolved from environment_id (no separate catalog param — FLINK_CATALOG is not required by connect()). Database is FLINK_DATABASE (cluster display name); pass database_kafka_cluster_id=KAFKA_CLUSTER_ID (the lkc-…) as well so the driver skips the CMK cluster-id lookup.

A thin, failure-tolerant wrapper mirroring FlinkSnapshotClient's posture (missing creds or any error → [], never raises; logs the reason). One method:

def query(self, sql: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Run one snapshot SELECT; return [{column: value}]. [] on any failure."""
  • Lists required settings (the connect() coordinates); if any is unset, log and return [] (same pattern as _missing_settings).
  • connect(organization_id=FLINK_ORG_ID, environment_id=FLINK_ENV_ID, cloud_provider=CLOUD_PROVIDER, cloud_region=CLOUD_REGION, compute_pool_id=FLINK_COMPUTE_POOL_ID, flink_api_key=FLINK_API_KEY, flink_api_secret=FLINK_API_SECRET, database=FLINK_DATABASE, database_kafka_cluster_id=KAFKA_CLUSTER_ID).
  • Required-settings list therefore adds CLOUD_PROVIDER and CLOUD_REGION (today optional, set only for RTCE/Lightning). This couples analytics-live to those being provisioned — see "What's left to the builder".

docs.title: CEP Fraud Scenarios — Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-30 Status: Draft for approval Repo: stream_house_c360_demo

docs.title: Intent & Why
docs.text:
The existing Flink pipeline is a pure analytics/aggregation DAG: CDC events flow through src_* → dim_* → fct_c360_profile, and everything downstream reads rolled-up aggregates (balances, totals) via snapshot queries. This is a solid streaming-analytics story, but it does not demonstrate Flink's Complex Event Processing (CEP) capability — pattern matching over ordered event sequences.

MATCH_RECOGNIZE is Flink SQL's native CEP clause. It detects user-defined event sequences within a partitioned, time-ordered stream. The canonical use case is fraud detection: a "card probe" (small test charge) immediately followed by one or more large charges on the same account is a well-known fraudster pattern. It is also the single clearest way to show the difference between batch analytics and streaming CEP in one demo.

This feature adds:

  1. A controlled scenario system — the backend can inject deterministic transaction sequences (not random) via a REST API, so a solution engineer can trigger a fraud sequence on demand.
  2. Three MATCH_RECOGNIZE Flink SQL models — one per CEP pattern — deployed alongside the existing c360 pipeline.
  3. A CEP page in the frontend that shows all three patterns, lets the SE fire a scenario with one click, and displays the matching events as they land.

The audience is an SE running a live demo. The demo narrative must be deterministic and self-contained (no random data generation, no waiting for organic traffic to accidentally form a pattern).

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• A POST /api/v1/scenarios/{scenario_id}/run endpoint triggers a controlled, scripted transaction sequence that is guaranteed to fire a MATCH_RECOGNIZE query.
  • Three CEP patterns are defined as dbt/Flink SQL models: fct_fraud_probe, fct_merchant_streak, fct_smb_spike.
  • A new CEP page in the frontend (/cep) lists the three patterns, lets the SE pick one, trigger it, and see the matched events.
  • The scenario system is self-contained — it only needs SINK=postgres and the existing Kafka path. No new infra dependencies.
  • CEP_DATA_MODE: mock | live mirrors the other mode toggles: mock returns a deterministic canned result; live injects real transactions and reads matched events from Flink.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Changing the existing fct_c360_profile / analytics pipeline. The three new Flink models are additions, not replacements.
  • A general-purpose "replay" or "load test" tool — only the specific scripted patterns are exposed.
  • A streaming WebSocket push from Flink to the browser. The CEP page polls the backend.
  • Per-customer alert routing or notification logic — this is a demo page, not production alerting.

docs.title: Anti-Goals
docs.text:
• A scenario that relies on random timing or random amounts to trigger the match. Every scenario is fully scripted (account ID, amounts, timestamps, sequence).
  • A demo that requires the SE to wait >30 seconds to see a match. Scripted injection lets the match land within the Flink window.
  • Secrets in the frontend — all Confluent/Kafka calls go through the backend.

docs.title: Domain Model Changes (prerequisite, in progress)
docs.text:
The following CSV-level changes are already being applied as a separate task:

Change Effect on CEP Segment renamed RETAIL → PRIVATE fct_smb_spike can filter customer_segment = 'SMB' precisely Carter (00000000-0000-0000-0000-ef1234567890) gets a second account (SAV-39958839, SAVINGS, ACTIVE) Fraud probe fires on CHECKING; SAVINGS stays clean — demonstrates per-account isolation Duplicate Linda Sharma row removed Clean 10-row seed

These changes are prerequisites. The spec assumes them as done.

docs.title: Pattern 1 — Fraud Probe (fct_fraud_probe)
docs.text:
What it detects: On the same account, a small charge (amount ≤ $10 — a card-verification test) is immediately followed by one or more large charges (amount ≥ $500) within a 1-hour event-time window.

Why it matters: This is the classic card-cloning telltale. The fraudster tests a stolen card with a micro-charge, then immediately drains it.

Scenario triggering it (fraud-probe): 

Account: CHK-39958838 (Carter's CHECKING)
t+0s   DEBIT  $2.99   "Card verification"   Amazon     RETAIL  ONLINE
t+30s  DEBIT  $899.00 "Electronics"         Amazon     RETAIL  ONLINE
t+60s  DEBIT  $749.00 "Gift cards"          Amazon     RETAIL  ONLINE
Carter's SAVINGS account (SAV-39958839) gets a benign $45 grocery charge at the same time — the query must not match it.

Flink SQL sketch: 

SELECT * FROM src_transactions
MATCH_RECOGNIZE (
    PARTITION BY account_id
    ORDER BY transacted_at
    MEASURES
        PROBE.account_id       AS account_id,
        PROBE.transacted_at    AS probe_time,
        LAST(LARGE.amount)     AS last_large_amount,
        COUNT(LARGE.*)         AS large_count
    ONE ROW PER MATCH
    AFTER MATCH SKIP TO NEXT ROW
    PATTERN (PROBE LARGE+)
    WITHIN INTERVAL '1' HOUR
    DEFINE
        PROBE AS amount <= 10.00,
        LARGE AS amount >= 500.00
)

docs.title: Pattern 2 — Merchant Streak (fct_merchant_streak)
docs.text:
What it detects: A customer makes 3 or more consecutive transactions in the same merchant category (e.g. three FOOD charges in a row). Signals a habit or a loyalty opportunity.

Why it matters: Demonstrates CEP for engagement/loyalty analytics, not just fraud. Shows MATCH_RECOGNIZE is general-purpose.

Scenario triggering it (merchant-streak): 

Customer: Maria Gonzalez (00000000-0000-0000-0000-f01234567891)
Account:  CHK-83197857
t+0s   DEBIT  $12.50  "Coffee"              Starbucks  FOOD  POS
t+5m   DEBIT  $34.00  "Team lunch"          Chipotle   FOOD  POS
t+10m  DEBIT  $89.00  "Client dinner"       Nobu       FOOD  POS

Flink SQL sketch: 

SELECT * FROM src_transactions
MATCH_RECOGNIZE (
    PARTITION BY customer_id
    ORDER BY transacted_at
    MEASURES
        FIRST(A.customer_id)         AS customer_id,
        FIRST(A.merchant_category)   AS streak_category,
        FIRST(A.transacted_at)       AS streak_start,
        LAST(A.transacted_at)        AS streak_end,
        COUNT(A.*)                   AS streak_length
    ONE ROW PER MATCH
    AFTER MATCH SKIP PAST LAST ROW
    PATTERN (A{3,})
    WITHIN INTERVAL '2' HOUR
    DEFINE
        A AS (COUNT(A.*) = 1
              OR A.merchant_category = LAST(A.merchant_category))
)

docs.title: Pattern 3 — SMB Spike (fct_smb_spike)
docs.text:
What it detects: An SMB customer makes 3 consecutive large charges (amount ≥ $200) followed by a CREDIT (refund or expense reversal) on the same account. Signals a business expense dispute or an anomalous spike worth flagging for the relationship manager.

Why it matters: Ties the PRIVATE vs SMB segment distinction directly to a business-relevant pattern. Shows MATCH_RECOGNIZE working with a join to customer context.

Scenario triggering it (smb-spike): 

Customer: David Okafor (00000000-0000-0000-0000-234567890124) — SMB
Account:  CHK-39587039  (re-activated as ACTIVE for this demo)
t+0s   DEBIT  $420.00  "Office supplies"    Staples    RETAIL   POS
t+5m   DEBIT  $380.00  "Cloud software"     AWS        RETAIL   ONLINE
t+10m  DEBIT  $610.00  "Hardware"           Apple      RETAIL   ONLINE
t+15m  CREDIT $1200.00 "Expense reversal"   Acme Corp  INCOME   ONLINE

Flink SQL sketch: 

SELECT * FROM src_transactions t
JOIN src_customers c ON t.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE c.customer_segment = 'SMB'
MATCH_RECOGNIZE (
    PARTITION BY t.account_id
    ORDER BY t.transacted_at
    MEASURES
        FIRST(LARGE.account_id)   AS account_id,
        FIRST(LARGE.transacted_at) AS spike_start,
        SUM(LARGE.amount)          AS spike_total,
        REV.amount                 AS reversal_amount
    ONE ROW PER MATCH
    AFTER MATCH SKIP TO NEXT ROW
    PATTERN (LARGE{3,} REV)
    WITHIN INTERVAL '1' HOUR
    DEFINE
        LARGE AS transaction_type = 'DEBIT' AND amount >= 200.00,
        REV   AS transaction_type = 'CREDIT'
)

Note to builder: Flink SQL's MATCH_RECOGNIZE applies after all joins and filters in the containing query. The exact placement of the WHERE clause and join with src_customers must be verified against the Confluent Cloud Flink SQL dialect at implementation time. An alternative is to pre-join in a CTE.

docs.title: registry.py
docs.text:
A module-level SCENARIOS: dict[str, ScenarioDefinition] populated at import time with the three hard-coded scenario definitions above. No database, no file — the sequences are committed Python literals. UUIDs for account_id and customer_id are the seed values from the CSV (so they resolve against real rows in Postgres).

The offset_seconds field allows the runner to shift all timestamps relative to datetime.now(utc) so every scenario "just happened" whenever it is triggered.

docs.title: runner.py
docs.text:
def build_transactions(
    defn: ScenarioDefinition,
    now: datetime | None = None,
) -> list[TransactionCreate]:
    """Materialise the scripted sequence into TransactionCreate rows,
    shifting offset_seconds relative to now."""

Pure function (no I/O). Returns list[TransactionCreate] ready for the sink. Deterministic given the same now and the same ScenarioDefinition.

docs.title: service.py
docs.text:
def run(scenario_id: str) -> ScenarioResult:
    """Look up the scenario, build rows, write to DB, publish to Kafka."""
  • Resolves from registry.SCENARIOS; raises UnknownScenarioError if not found.
  • Calls runner.build_transactions(defn) → list[TransactionCreate].
  • Delegates to transactions.db_sink.create_many(txns) (same path as the generate endpoint — no new DB logic).
  • If KAFKA_PRODUCE_ENABLED and not CDC_CONNECTOR_ENABLED: calls transactions.kafka_producer.produce_create_many(txns) (same Kafka path).
  • Returns ScenarioResult with the inserted Transaction rows.

docs.title: Flink SQL Models (new, under pipelines/)
docs.text:
Three new dbt models in pipelines/models/c360/facts/:

pipelines/models/c360/facts/
├── fct_fraud_probe.sql
├── fct_fraud_probe.yml
├── fct_merchant_streak.sql
├── fct_merchant_streak.yml
├── fct_smb_spike.sql

All three are materialized_table with: - changelog.mode: append (each match is a new row — matches are never retracted) - kafka.cleanup-policy: delete - scan.startup.mode: earliest-offset - value.format: avro-registry

They are added to deploy_manifest.json under the existing pipeline group, after the src_* and dim_* layers they depend on.

The exact Flink SQL syntax (particularly join placement for Pattern 3 and the DEFINE clause details) must be validated against the Confluent Cloud Flink SQL reference before deployment. The sketches above are design-intent, not final SQL.

docs.text:
1. Scenarios are committed Python literals, not DB records. They don't need CRUD — they are part of the demo script. If a new pattern is needed, it is added in code, not via an admin UI.

  2. POST .../run returns the injected Transaction rows, not the Flink match output. Flink match output is polled separately (mock: canned; live: queries the fct_fraud_probe topic). This keeps the injection path fast and synchronous, while the "did Flink fire?" check is async.

  5. Pattern SQL is design-intent, not final. The Confluent Cloud Flink SQL dialect imposes constraints on MATCH_RECOGNIZE placement within a query (especially with joins). The builder must validate each sketch against the reference docs before writing the .sql files.

docs.title: Intent & why
docs.text:
The StatementGraphPage shows a data product's Flink pipeline as a graph of statements. This feature adds a cost banner at the top of that page showing the month-to-date dollar cost of the whole pipeline, computed from the Confluent Cloud Cost API.

The point is a demonstration: prove that we can attribute real billed dollars to a complete Flink pipeline by mapping each statement to its compute pool and consolidating the pools' cost from the Cost API. It is a credibility/story feature for prospects, not an internal spend-monitoring tool.

Billing is pool-level in Confluent (CFUs are billed per compute pool, not per statement), so the design models cost at compute-pool granularity and attributes it to a product via a statement→pool mapping sourced from dbt.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Display one aggregated cost figure per data product at the top of StatementGraphPage: $<amount> this month · <N> CFU (decision: banner format B).
  • Attribute cost by collecting the distinct compute pool ids used by the product's own statements and summing this-month Flink cost for those pools.
  • Model two compute pools: the existing pool for c360, a new pool for crm, so the demo shows two products with genuinely different pools and costs.
  • Keep the mechanism general: cost consolidation is driven by per-statement compute_pool_id in the descriptor, not hardcoded per product.
  • Work in mock mode with a synthetic cost (decision: yes), so the demo runs with no live cloud or billing access.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Per-statement dollar attribution. The Cost API bills per pool; splitting a pool across statements would be invented numbers. Out of scope.
  • Historical cost charts, trends, or time-series. One current month-to-date number only.
  • Cost alerting, budgets, or forecasting.
  • Non-Flink cost (Kafka, Connect, SR, etc.). Only product = FLINK line items.

docs.title: Anti-goals (what makes this a failure even if it "works")
docs.text:
• A number that silently double-counts or misattributes cost across products (e.g. counting the shared fct_c360_profile upstream node toward crm). The shared node MUST be excluded from crm (decision: exclude).
  • A banner that breaks or blanks the page when the Cost API is slow, returns no data for the current (lagging) day, or the principal lacks billing access. Cost is best-effort; its absence must degrade gracefully, never break the graph.
  • Hand-edited descriptor JSON that the next build_descriptors.py run silently overwrites.

docs.title: Constraints & facts that shape the design
docs.text:
• Descriptor JSONs are generated from the dbt manifest.json by scripts/build_descriptors.py + apps/backend/data_products/descriptor_builder.py. Any new node field must be emitted by the builder, not hand-written into c360.json / crm.json.
  • dbt supports per-model compute_pool_id (_UNIVERSAL_CONFIG_KEYS in the confluent adapter). Unset models inherit the profile default (~/.dbt/profiles.yml → FLINK_COMPUTE_POOL_ID).
  • Cost API GET /billing/v1/costs:
  • Required query params start_date, end_date (dates); page_size (≤10000, default 5000) + page_token pagination. Granularity is DAILY — one line item per resource per day per line_type.
  • Line item fields used: product (filter == FLINK), line_type (FLINK_NUM_CFUS), resource.id (the compute pool id, lfcp-…), resource.environment.id, amount (post-discount dollars), quantity, unit, start_date/end_date.
  • Auth: Cloud API key via HTTP Basic — same auth=(key, secret) httpx pattern as the existing Metrics client.
  • "This month" = start_date = first day of current month (UTC), end_date = today (UTC). Sum amount across days for the target pool ids.
  • Cost data lags ~a day. The banner changes slowly; it must poll on a slow interval, independent of the 5s status poll.
  • Open risk (confirm during build): the doc's resource.id examples list Kafka/Connect/SR/ksqlDB but do not explicitly spell out the Flink compute-pool form. If live Flink cost turns out to be reported only at environment granularity (no per-pool resource.id), per-pool consolidation degrades to per-environment. Mitigation: the builder confirms against a real response; mock mode keeps the demo safe regardless. See "Live verification" below.

docs.title: Decisions already made (by the owner)
docs.text:
1. Granularity: compute-pool level (not per-statement approximation).
  2. Banner format B: $<amount> this month · <N> CFU.
  3. Mock mode shows a synthetic cost: yes.
  4. Shared upstream node excluded: crm cost excludes fct_c360_profile (count only each product's own statements' pools).
  5. Two pools: existing pool = c360; new pool = crm.
  6. The owner runs terraform apply; this work authors the TF + wiring only.
  7. Billing role to Terraform: add an org-level billing-read role binding for the Cost API principal in the TF (vs. mock-only or manual grant).

docs.title: The "N CFU" value in the banner
docs.text: The banner's · <N> CFU is the current total CFUs across the product's compute pool(s), not a billing figure. Source it the same way the existing per-node metrics drill-down already gets compute_pool_cfu (Metrics API, io.confluent.flink/compute_pool_utilization/current_cfus), summed over the distinct pools. In mock mode it is a synthetic constant consistent with the synthetic cost. (Builder's call: if wiring live current-CFU per pool proves heavier than expected, N may be sourced from the already-fetched per-statement metrics the page holds; the displayed semantics — "current CFU for this pipeline" — stay the same.)

docs.title: 1. Terraform (IaC/ccloud/)
docs.text:
• Add resource "confluent_flink_compute_pool" "crm_pool" in flink.tf mirroring the existing pool (same cloud/region/environment, display_name = "${var.prefix}-crm-flink-pool").
  • Add variable "flink_crm_max_cfu" in variables.tf next to flink_max_cfu (same default, e.g. 50).
  • Add output "flink_crm_compute_pool_id" in outputs.tf next to flink_compute_pool_id. Keep flink_compute_pool_id as the c360/default pool.
  • The existing Flink service account and API key are shared and need no change for the second pool (API keys are env+region scoped).
  • Billing role (decided): add a confluent_role_binding granting the principal used by the Cost API (CONFLUENT_CLOUD_API_KEY) an org-level billing/cost read role, bound at the organization CRN. Exact role name confirmed at build time (see "Billing role access" below). Enables the live real-dollars path on apply.

docs.title: 2. Env bridge
docs.text:
• scripts/set_env_from_tf.sh: add an export of FLINK_CRM_COMPUTE_POOL_ID from the new output (~line 56) and a matching entry in the env-dict that rewrites apps/backend/.env (~line 131).
  • apps/backend/.env.example: document FLINK_CRM_COMPUTE_POOL_ID in the live section.
  • apps/backend/config.py: add FLINK_CRM_COMPUTE_POOL_ID to Settings, and include it (masked/plain as appropriate) in summary()/log_summary().

docs.title: 3. dbt (pipelines/)
docs.text:
• Set compute_pool_id for the crm models so they resolve to the crm pool. Two acceptable spellings (builder picks the cleaner for this repo):
  • per-model config(compute_pool_id="{{ env_var('FLINK_CRM_COMPUTE_POOL_ID') }}") in each models/crm/**/*.sql, or
  • a folder-level block under models: in pipelines/dbt_project.yml for the crm path.
  • c360 models are left unset and inherit the profile default (FLINK_COMPUTE_POOL_ID).
  • dbt renders the env var at parse time, so manifest.json carries the resolved pool id in each model's config.

docs.title: 4. Descriptor generation
docs.text:
• Add compute_pool_id: str | None = None and external: bool = False to GraphNode (apps/backend/data_products/models.py). external marks a node that is an upstream import from another product (see cross-product note).
  • In descriptor_builder.py, emit compute_pool_id for statement nodes. Reading the pool (resolves builder-check #3): the per-model pool must land in the serialized manifest config. The current manifest has no compute_pool_id config key on any model, and it is unverified whether a per-model config(compute_pool_id=…) promotes into node.config for this adapter version. Therefore:
  • Prefer setting the crm pool via a folder-level block in dbt_project.yml (models: streamhouse: crm: +compute_pool_id: …), which reliably serializes into each node's config — more robust than per-model config() for the manifest read.
  • Builder reads node.config["compute_pool_id"]; if absent, falls back to node.config.get("meta", {}) then to the profile/default pool (FLINK_COMPUTE_POOL_ID).
  • Build-time verification gate: after dbt run, confirm the crm nodes' manifest config actually carries the crm pool id before trusting the read. If neither config nor meta surfaces it, fall back to a builder-side product→pool env mapping (crm → FLINK_CRM_COMPUTE_POOL_ID, default otherwise) so attribution never silently collapses to one pool.
  • Cross-product upstream (resolves builder-check #1 — call made, see handover): crm.json today contains fct_c360_profile, a node the current builder cannot emit — it only emits same-product or source dependencies, so a naive regen would drop that node and all crm edges. Extend descriptor_builder.py so a dependency on a model from another product is emitted as a node+edge marked external: true, is_product: false, with the owning product's pool as its compute_pool_id. This (a) makes crm.json reproducible by the generator, and (b) provides the exact owned/external discriminator the anti-double-count rule needs. Note: this changes the committed crm.json — fct_c360_profile becomes external: true instead of its current (misleading) is_product: true; the crm graph still renders it as upstream.
  • Regenerate c360.json / crm.json via scripts/build_descriptors.py. Do not hand-edit the JSONs.

docs.title: 5. Backend cost path
docs.text:
• Client (apps/backend/data_products/confluent_client.py): add get_org_costs(start_date, end_date) -> list[dict] (or a focused get_flink_pool_costs) using httpx.get against https://api.confluent.cloud/billing/v1/costs, auth=(CONFLUENT_CLOUD_API_KEY, CONFLUENT_CLOUD_API_SECRET), paginating on page_token. Best-effort: catch httpx.HTTPError/ValueError, return []. Filter to product == FLINK.
  • Model (models.py): CostResponse { amount: float, currency: str = "USD", cfu: float | None, period_start: date, period_end: date, pool_ids: list[str], available: bool }. available=False signals "no cost to show" so the frontend can hide rather than render $0.
  • Provider (providers.py): add get_cost(graph) -> CostResponse to both:
  • LiveProvider: collect distinct compute_pool_id from the graph's statement nodes (excluding non-owned upstream — see below), call the client for this month, sum amount for those pool ids, attach summed current CFU.
  • MockProvider: return a deterministic synthetic CostResponse (plausible amount + CFU), available=True.
  • Service (data_products/service.py): get_cost(product_id) loads the descriptor and delegates to the active provider.
  • Route (api/data_product_resource.py): GET /data-products/{id}/cost → CostResponse.

"Product's own statements" rule (anti-double-count): when collecting pool ids, include a statement node only if type == "statement" AND external == False. The external marker (emitted by the builder, see §4) is the single discriminator — fct_c360_profile inside crm.json is external: true and so its (c360) pool is never counted toward crm. Observable result MUST be: crm's cost counts only the crm pool, c360's counts only the c360 pool.

docs.title: 5b. Make the existing metrics path pool-aware (required by the pool split)
docs.text: Resolves builder-check #2 — a correctness fix, not just a new feature. The existing live status/metrics drill-down hardcodes the single default pool in its Metrics API queries (confluent_client.py get_statement_metrics / get_materialized_table_metrics, using settings.FLINK_COMPUTE_POOL_ID). Once crm statements run on the crm pool, those per-node queries for crm nodes would target the wrong pool and return empty/403 — a silent regression of the existing feature. Fix: thread each node's compute_pool_id (now present on the descriptor node) through the metrics/status calls, falling back to FLINK_COMPUTE_POOL_ID when a node has none. This is in scope and is a prerequisite for the two-pool demo working live. (Call made — see handover; it enlarges the backend change beyond the banner itself.)

docs.title: 6. Frontend
docs.text:
• types/dataProduct.ts: add Cost type mirroring CostResponse.
  • api/dataProducts.ts: getCost(id) → GET /data-products/{id}/cost.
  • StatementGraphPage.tsx: fetch cost on mount and on a slow interval (e.g. 5 min; cost lags ~a day), render in the .page-header / .health-bar as $<amount> this month · <N> CFU. When available === false or the fetch fails, hide the banner (no $0, no error) — the graph is unaffected.
  • Format via existing lib/format.ts (add a currency formatter if none).

docs.title: Billing role access — DECIDED: add to Terraform
docs.text:
The feature's premise is showing real billed dollars. The existing CONFLUENT_CLOUD_API_KEY principal is provisioned for MetricsViewer; the Cost API (/billing/v1/costs) needs an org-level billing read role.

Decision (owner): add the billing role binding to the Terraform. §1 adds a confluent_role_binding granting the principal org-level cost/billing read, so terraform apply enables the real-dollars live path. Applying this binding may itself require org-admin privileges on the account running apply — the owner runs apply. The exact role name (e.g. OrganizationAdmin, or a dedicated billing/metrics-billing role if available on this org) is confirmed at build time, since Confluent's granular billing-read role availability varies by org; the binding targets the organization CRN of the existing Flink service account principal.

docs.title: Live verification (resolves the open risk)
docs.text:
During build, against the live environment, fetch one real GET /billing/v1/costs response for a day with Flink usage and confirm that product == FLINK line items carry the compute pool id in resource.id (lfcp-…). If confirmed, the per-pool design stands as written. If Flink cost is only environment-granular, record it here and fall back to per-environment attribution (the two-pool demo still differentiates products only if the pools are in different environments — if not, document the limitation and lean on mock mode for the demo). This verification gates the live path; mock mode ships regardless.

Status (2026-10-30): PENDING — owner action. The implementation shipped with mock mode fully working and the live path best-effort (hidden on 403/empty). The live granularity check could not be run during build: it needs the crm compute pool applied (terraform apply), the billing role granted, and real Flink usage to bill against — none available in the build environment. Owner to run after applying the infra: fetch one GET /billing/v1/costs day with Flink usage, confirm product == FLINK items carry the pool id in resource.id, and record the outcome here. Also refresh the committed descriptors (dbt run + scripts/build_descriptors.py) so their compute_pool_id values are the real pool ids rather than the build-time placeholders (lfcp-c360 / lfcp-crm).

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Backend unit tests mirroring existing tests/: descriptor builder emits compute_pool_id with correct fallback; provider get_cost sums only the owned pools and excludes the shared upstream; mock provider returns a stable synthetic CostResponse; cost route shape. Client HTTP is mocked (httpx), asserting the Cost API query params (start_date/end_date/paging) and the FLINK + pool-id filtering.
  • Frontend: a light test/manual check that the banner renders format B and hides when available === false.

docs.title: What's left to the builder
docs.text:
• Exact dbt spelling (per-model config() vs dbt_project.yml folder block).
  • The precise "owned statement" signal in the descriptor (reuse is_product / folder, or add an explicit marker) — subject to the fixed observable result.
  • How live current-CFU per pool is summed for the banner's N CFU, vs reusing metrics the page already holds.
  • Synthetic values for mock mode.
  • Currency formatting helper details.
